/-!
# Conjecture 5.59

by B. Hartley

Let $G$ be a locally finite group which is the product of a $p$-subgroup and a
$q$-subgroup, where $p$ and $q$ are distinct primes. Is $G$ a $\{p, q\}$-group?

Here a group is *locally finite* if every finitely generated subgroup is finite.
A $p$-group is a group in which every element has order a power of $p$, and a
$\{p, q\}$-group is a group in which every element has order of the form $p^a q^b$.
"$G$ is the product of $P$ and $Q$" means $G = PQ = \{xy : x \in P,\ y \in Q\}$ as a set;
the subgroups $P$ and $Q$ are not assumed to be normal.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

def IsLocallyFinite (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG → Finite H

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsLocallyFinite.isOfFinOrder {G : Type*} [Group G] (hG : IsLocallyFinite G) (g : G) :
    IsOfFinOrder g := by
  have : Finite (Subgroup.zpowers g) := hG _ ⟨{g}, by simp [Subgroup.zpowers_eq_closure]⟩
  obtain ⟨n, hn, hgn⟩ :=
    (isOfFinOrder_of_finite (⟨g, Subgroup.mem_zpowers g⟩ : Subgroup.zpowers g)).exists_pow_eq_one
  exact isOfFinOrder_iff_pow_eq_one.mpr ⟨n, hn, by simpa using congrArg Subtype.val hgn⟩

claims.decomposer_note: Single yes/no question, implicitly universally quantified over all locally finite G (every finitely generated subgroup finite), all distinct primes p, q and all subgroups P, Q with G = PQ as a set product (P, Q need not be normal, and P, Q are p-/q-groups in the sense that every element has p-/q-power order); the conclusion '{p,q}-group' means every element of G has order divisible only by the primes p and q (equivalently, for locally finite G, every finite subgroup has order of the form p^a q^b).
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the same faithful proposition: answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ G : Type [Group G], locally finite (∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG → Finite H) → ∀ distinct primes p q, ∀ subgroups P Q with IsPGroup p ↥P, IsPGroup q ↥Q and (P : Set G) * (Q : Set G) = Set.univ (set product G = PQ, no normality) → every g has orderOf g = p^a * q^b. I verified IsPGroup unfolds to 'every element has p-power order' (correct for infinite subgroups) and that the pointwise set product equality is exactly ∀ g, ∃ x ∈ P, ∃ y ∈ Q, x*y = g. The conclusion encodings (orderOf g = p^a q^b in c01/c04/c05/c06/c07; g^(p^a q^b) = 1 in c02/c03; prime divisors of orderOf g in {p,q} in c08) are all equivalent under local finiteness and none has an orderOf = 0 loophole. c05 was chosen for style: bespoke IsLocallyFinite with two API lemmas (finite ⇒ locally finite; locally finite ⇒ every element has finite order, which documents why the orderOf encoding is safe), hypotheses in the statement's order, [Group G] binder as in Kourovka/1_40 and 19_25, v46 reference URL as required. Used essentially verbatim (minor docstring tweak); compiles with only the 'declaration uses sorry' warning.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 5.59

by B. Hartley

Let $G$ be a locally finite group which is the product of a $p$-subgroup and a
$q$-subgroup, where $p$ and $q$ are distinct primes. Is $G$ a $\{p, q\}$-group?

Here a group is *locally finite* if every finitely generated subgroup is finite.
A $p$-group is a group in which every element has order a power of $p$, and a
$\{p, q\}$-group is a group in which every element has order of the form $p^a q^b$.
"$G$ is the product of $P$ and $Q$" means $G = PQ = \{xy : x \in P,\ y \in Q\}$ as a set;
the subgroups $P$ and $Q$ are not assumed to be normal.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

open scoped Pointwise

namespace Kourovka.«5.59»

/-- A group is *locally finite* if every finitely generated subgroup is finite. -/
def IsLocallyFinite (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG → Finite H

/-- Every finite group is locally finite. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsLocallyFinite.of_finite (G : Type*) [Group G] [Finite G] : IsLocallyFinite G :=
  fun _ _ => inferInstance

/-- Every element of a locally finite group has finite order. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsLocallyFinite.isOfFinOrder {G : Type*} [Group G] (hG : IsLocallyFinite G) (g : G) :
    IsOfFinOrder g := by
  have : Finite (Subgroup.zpowers g) := hG _ ⟨{g}, by simp [Subgroup.zpowers_eq_closure]⟩
  obtain ⟨n, hn, hgn⟩ :=
    (isOfFinOrder_of_finite (⟨g, Subgroup.mem_zpowers g⟩ : Subgroup.zpowers g)).exists_pow_eq_one
  exact isOfFinOrder_iff_pow_eq_one.mpr ⟨n, hn, by simpa using congrArg Subtype.val hgn⟩

/--
Let $G$ be a locally finite group which is the product of a $p$-subgroup and a
$q$-subgroup, where $p$ and $q$ are distinct primes. Is $G$ a $\{p, q\}$-group?

Here $G$ is the product of the subgroups $P$ and $Q$ if $G = PQ$ as a set, i.e.
every element of $G$ is of the form $xy$ with $x \in P$ and $y \in Q$; the subgroups
$P$ and $Q$ need not be normal. A $p$-group is a group in which every element has
order a power of $p$ (`IsPGroup`), and $G$ is a $\{p, q\}$-group if every element of
$G$ has order of the form $p^a q^b$ for some $a, b \geq 0$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«5.59» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsLocallyFinite G →
      ∀ (p q : ℕ), p.Prime → q.Prime → p ≠ q →
      ∀ (P Q : Subgroup G), IsPGroup p P → IsPGroup q Q →
      (P : Set G) * (Q : Set G) = Set.univ →
      ∀ g : G, ∃ a b : ℕ, orderOf g = p ^ a * q ^ b := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«5.59»

items: 'G is the product of a p-subgroup and a q-subgroup' is modeled as the set product (P : Set G) * (Q : Set G) = Set.univ with P, Q arbitrary (not necessarily normal) subgroups, matching the decomposition notes; not as P ⊔ Q = ⊤, which would be weaker.
'p-subgroup' uses Mathlib's IsPGroup p P (every element has p-power order), which is the correct notion for possibly infinite groups; p and q are only required to be distinct primes.

'{p,q}-group' is stated directly as ∀ g, ∃ a b, orderOf g = p^a * q^b rather than via a general π-group definition. Since p, q are primes, p^a q^b ≠ 0, so infinite-order elements (orderOf = 0) are excluded automatically; under the locally finite hypothesis this is also the same as 'every finite subgroup has order p^a q^b'.
Locally finite is defined as every finitely generated subgroup (Subgroup.FG) being finite; an equivalent alternative would be Finite (Subgroup.closure S) for every finite S.

The bespoke definition is placed in the problem file (as in Kourovka/1_40.lean) because the task restricts output to a single file; a reviewer may prefer moving IsLocallyFinite to FormalConjecturesForMathlib as reusable mathematics.
G is quantified over Type (not Type*), following the convention of the other Kourovka files.

reviewer_notes: No ambiguity of substance: 'product of a p-subgroup and a q-subgroup' is read as G = PQ setwise for arbitrary (not necessarily normal) subgroups, which is the standard meaning in factorized-group problems and matches the decomposition notes; using P ⊔ Q = ⊤ would have been wrong (weaker hypothesis, stronger claim) and no candidate did that. The bespoke IsLocallyFinite is generic and would ideally live in FormalConjecturesForMathlib per STATEMENTS.md; it is kept in the problem file because the deliverable is a single file (precedent: Kourovka/1_40.lean). answer(True) = 'yes, every such G is a {p,q}-group'; answer(False) = a counterexample exists. Boundary cases: trivial G satisfies the conclusion (orderOf 1 = p^0 q^0); no hypothesis is unsatisfiable. G is quantified over Type (universe 0), following the other Kourovka files.
